newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Q3 economic growth lowest in three years.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Q3 economic growth lowest in three years.

text.p: South Korea on Thursday posted its lowest quarterly economic growth in three years and economists said falling export prices coupled with sluggish capital investment would keep the economy in low gear until next year.

"A slump in exports is mainly to blame for the slowdown," said Paeng Dong-joon, director of the Bank of Korea's (BOK) statistics division. "Conditions are unlikely to improve until the middle of 1997."

The BOK, the central bank, said gross domestic product (GDP) grew a real 6.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996, the lowest quarterly growth since the second quarter of 1993, when it grew by 4.9 percent.
The growth compared with a 9.8 percent rise a year earlier and a 6.8 percent gain in the second quarter of this year.
Third-quarter exports rose 9.4 percent, sharply lower than 28.3 percent a year before, the central bank said. Imports rose 11.7 percent against 25.2 percent.
Paeng said a drastic slowdown in the sectors of agriculture, forestry and fishing, services and construction contributed to the poor performance in the third quarter.

Output in the agricultural, forestry and fishing sector increased 1.8 percent, down from a 6.4 percent rise a year earlier. The growth rate fell to 4.7 percent from 10.9 percent for the construction sector and to 7.7 percent from 10.8 percent for the service sector.
But Paeng and private-sector economists agreed GDP growth would be around seven percent for all of this year as the fourth quarter economy would be backed by robust rice crops.
GDP, which is the value of goods and services produced over a given period excluding income from overseas, grew by 9.0 percent in 1995.
Rice output rose 13 percent to 5.3 million tonnes this year from 4.7 million last year thanks to favourable weather, according to government statistics.
Economists said there were no signs the manufacturing sector, which grew only 7.0 percent in the third quarter against a 11.7 percent rise a year earlier, was turning around.
Capital investment, an indicator for future industrial activity, rose a year-on-year 8.7 percent in the third quarter, down sharply from a rise of 22.2 percent a year earlier.
Economists said plunging international prices for semiconductors, steel products and petrochemicals hit South Korea's major exports this year.

The unit price for the 16 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips fell 70 to 80 percent from about $50 a year ago. Memory chips accounted for about 20 percent of South Korea's total exports last year.
The Electronics Industries Association of Korea has said the country's electronics exports were expected to post the first drop in 14 years this year due to depressed chip exports.
It put this year's electronics exports at $41.67 billion, down from $43.59 billion in 1995.
"The export slump reduced consumers' purchasing power and slowed overall economy," said Kim Joon-il, an economist at the state think-tank Korea Development Institute.
"The price shock was so serious that the economic slowdown was felt more strongly than the 6.4 percent growth indicated."
Private-sector consumption rose 6.0 percent, against an 8.0 percent rise a year earlier and a 7.1 percent rise in the second quarter.
